title: TE-6 — Default Content Detail Presentation Delivery
summary: let a dedicated single-table document enter Content Detail View as its initial presentation without flashing the ordinary document or visibly changing layout after content appears
content_html:
TE-6 — Default Content Detail Presentation Delivery

Status And Purpose

Proposed as TE-6, sequenced after TE-5 but dependent only on TE-3 establishing the public-safe content-detail view, exact table targets, expanded-main layout, return context, and cleanup lifecycle.

The delivery lets an ordinary document declare that its one authored Markdown table is its preferred initial presentation. It is intended for dedicated child documents reached through a parent’s ordinary More… link, but it adds no special parent/child runtime relationship. Its defining requirement is a coordinated entry sequence: the reader must not see the normal document appear briefly and then resize or switch into Content Detail View.

Complete Outcome

A public or Manage document with the validated presentation hint opens directly into the existing table Content Detail View from an ordinary document link, sidebar, search result, Recent result, direct URL, reload, history traversal, cold payload fetch, or payload cache hit.

The route and index metadata identify the intended presentation before document rendering begins. Docs Viewer projects the final expanded-main geometry while the destination is pending, prepares the ordinary rendered HTML outside the visible and accessible presentation, resolves its sole eligible table through the TE-3 adapter, and reveals the Content Detail table in one coordinated commit. No frame exposes the destination’s ordinary document before the detail view, and the visible panel does not change width after the table appears.

Back to document reveals the already-prepared destination document without another fetch or Markdown render and suppresses the authored default for that current document visit. Browser Back still follows ordinary route history, so a parent More… link can return directly to the parent without adding a detail-view history entry.

Proposed Authoring And Projection Contract

The proposed scalar front-matter field is:

viewer_content_detail: table

TE-6.0 freezes the exact name. The first contract accepts only table, requires exactly one eligible table in document-owned rendered HTML, and rejects unknown values or ambiguous documents during the Docs build. The field is projected into the index/tree document entry for preflight routing and repeated in the by-id payload for consistency validation. It is reader-safe and available to public and Manage composition.

The hint does not identify a table by heading, cell text, ordinal supplied by the author, or persistent ID. Build validation requires one authored Markdown table and implicitly projects the same data-docs-content-detail="table" eligibility marker established by TE-2; the author does not add a redundant table-detail comment. The single marked table is then registered from the existing rendered content_html by the TE-3 adapter. The parent uses a normal document link; link text such as More… is authoring choice rather than a new control.

Indexed Documents Only

The initial delivery applies only to documents represented in the active scope’s ordinary Docs index. This is a routing and ownership boundary, not a claim that sub-scope document content can never use Content Detail View.

A sub-scope document is absent from the parent index and remains embedded detail owned by its docs_subscope report. The selected Docs Viewer document is still the indexed parent report, subdoc is report-owned URL state, and the child payload renders only after the report and its manifest have loaded. TE-6’s ordinary index preflight therefore cannot know the child hint or exact table target before the report presentation begins.

A later exception would need a separately delivered report-to-Content-Detail contract: project the hint in the sub-scope manifest, let the report preflight the selected child, hand off an exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} table target, preserve list/detail/filter state, and solve direct-subdoc no-flash entry. TE-6 does not infer this behavior from child front matter or scan dynamic report DOM.

Flash-Free Rendering Sequence

The existing route flow normally selects rendered-document, clears the content mount for loading, inserts content_html, and then mounts document adapters. Reacting after that sequence would expose the ordinary document and cause a visible normal-to-expanded layout change. TE-6 instead freezes the following sequence:

  1. The router resolves the destination’s index entry and presentation hint before inspecting the payload cache or starting a fetch.
  2. The document-view coordinator records a new visit generation, selects the final expanded content-detail layout, clears the previous document, and projects one inert pending body at the final geometry. It must not select or reveal rendered-document as an intermediate view.
  3. A cached or fetched payload is passed through the existing Markdown-generated content_html path into a temporary non-visible preparation mount owned by the document lifecycle. The mount is excluded from focus, pointer interaction, live-region announcement, and the accessibility tree.
  4. Before dynamic document extras mount, the TE-3 table adapter validates and registers the sole eligible table against the current document target and visit generation.
  5. The coordinator commits the exact table target to the already-selected Content Detail View, replaces the pending body, and reveals the presentation. The expanded shell, toolbar position, and main-panel width are unchanged across that commit.
  6. After the first visible commit, ordinary diagram or report extras remain unmounted unless and until the user chooses Back to document. Back completes the prepared rendered-document mount, mounts its applicable extras, restores ordinary panel state, focuses the invocation destination where valid, and marks the default suppressed for the current visit before revealing it.
  7. Navigation, scope change, superseding payload request, build refresh, or disposal invalidates both the pending target and preparation mount through the existing request and document-mount generations.

TE-6.0 may select an equivalent staging mechanism, but it must preserve these observable guarantees. A second visible document pane, persistent hidden reader, parallel view host, full duplicate application mount, or CSS-only late concealment after the document has painted is not acceptable.

State, Failure, And History

  • The authored default applies once per fresh document visit. Explicit Back to document suppresses it before the ordinary document is revealed, preventing an immediate reopen loop.
  • The suppression owner and lifetime are frozen in TE-6.0. It must survive same-visit re-projection without becoming cross-document preference or persisted user state.
  • Content Detail entry does not push or replace route history. The canonical document URL remains the child document URL, so browser navigation keeps ordinary document semantics.
  • An unavailable view, stale generation, missing table, multiple tables, malformed payload, or adapter failure releases the pending state and atomically presents the ordinary document with an explicit error. It never selects an arbitrary table.
  • Cold loads and cache hits use the same preflight and commit sequence; the cache path must not bypass the no-flash guarantee.
  • Hash targets are incompatible with automatic table entry in the initial contract and must cause a defined ordinary-document fallback rather than applying an invisible scroll target.

Current Seams And Expected Size

The likely owners are Docs source/front-matter projection, index/tree and by-id payload metadata, the document router’s pre-cache navigation decision, route workflow, document-view coordinator, document controller, the TE-3 table adapter and target lifecycle, panel layout, a narrowly owned preparation state, and focused build/module/browser smoke.

The current indicative shape is 8–12 touched production files, approximately 450–750 production Python/JavaScript/CSS lines and 300–550 focused test lines. TE-6.0 must replace this estimate with exact build, router, coordinator, preparation, adapter, CSS, and test files before implementation. If the required shape introduces a second content mount as a durable reader, duplicates document extras, changes URL semantics, creates general per-document view routing, or materially exceeds the estimate, stop for review.

Rough Delivery Steps

TE-6.0 — Trace And Freeze Preflight And Commit

  • [ ] Trace cold and cached document navigation, loading-state projection, payload insertion, main-view selection, panel-layout projection, table registration, dynamic extras, history traversal, hash handling, request cancellation, and initial app startup in public and Manage readers.
  • [ ] Freeze the scalar authoring field, allowed value, exactly-one-table build validation, implicit TE-2 eligibility marker, public/index/tree/by-id projections, and unknown or invalid value failures.
  • [ ] Freeze the visit generation, default-suppression owner and lifetime, pending content semantics, hidden preparation mechanism, exact target handoff, atomic reveal, Back completion, error fallback, and cleanup order.
  • [ ] Freeze the visible invariant: final outer geometry is projected before destination content can paint; neither the destination’s ordinary document nor a normal-width table is visible or exposed to assistive technology before the detail presentation.
  • [ ] Record exact production/test files, reused TE-3 seams, and rough diffs for TE-6.1, TE-6.2, and TE-6.3 before implementation approval.

Checkpoint: an instrumented fixture with one large table demonstrates cold load, cache hit, parent More… navigation, direct URL, reload, browser Back/Forward, Back to document, slow payload, stale response, and invalid metadata. Frame-by-frame evidence shows stable expanded geometry and no visible ordinary-document interval. Stop before implementation.

TE-6.1 — Project And Validate The Document Hint

  • [ ] Add the frozen field to canonical document records and validate the supported value during Docs builds.
  • [ ] Validate that the rendered document owns exactly one eligible pre-extras Markdown table; fail the build for zero, multiple, dynamic-only, or otherwise unsupported targets.
  • [ ] Project the hint into the reader-safe index/tree entry and by-id payload and project the implicit table-detail marker onto its sole table without projecting unrelated management metadata.
  • [ ] Add focused source parsing, validation, public/local projection, targeted-build, and generated-payload tests.

TE-6.2 — Add Coordinated Default Entry

  • [ ] Let the router pass the indexed presentation intent into navigation preflight before both payload-cache and fetch branches.
  • [ ] Extend the existing coordinator and panel-layout lifecycle with the frozen pending-to-content-detail commit; do not register another main view or route.
  • [ ] Prepare the existing rendered HTML without visual or accessible exposure, then request the exact table target through the TE-3 adapter.
  • [ ] Make the cached and cold paths share the same target validation, atomic reveal, cancellation, and fallback behavior.
  • [ ] Implement Back to document completion and same-visit suppression before ordinary content is revealed, without adding a history entry or refetching the payload.
  • [ ] Release preparation, target, listeners, and suppression state on the frozen lifecycle boundaries.

TE-6.3 — Verify And Transfer

  • [ ] Run focused build projection, router, cache/fetch parity, coordinator, panel-layout, target-generation, Back suppression, history, hash fallback, stale response, failure, public/Manage import-boundary, lint, generated Docs/search, and whitespace checks.
  • [ ] Use an intentionally slow payload plus frame/geometry instrumentation to verify that the destination ordinary document never paints and the visible main panel does not resize after the table appears.
  • [ ] Manually review parent More… navigation, sidebar, search, Recent, direct URL, reload, Back/Forward, Back to document, light/dark, narrow/wide, public/Manage, focus order, screen-reader exposure, and invalid configuration fallback.
  • [ ] Prove ordinary documents, manually opened tables, dynamic reports, diagrams, source mode, Review, and documents without the hint retain their existing behavior.
  • [ ] Update the durable document metadata, panel/view lifecycle, and Content Detail authorities with the shipped field and preflight/commit contract.

Not In Scope

  • automatic detail presentation for multiple tables, a selected ordinal, diagrams, media, reports, search results, or arbitrary content kinds;
  • sub-scope documents rendered as docs_subscope embedded detail; a future exception requires an explicit report-owned preflight and restoration delivery;
  • a special More… component, inferred parent/child relationship, automatic summary-table generation, or source splitting;
  • stable table IDs, table fragments, detail query parameters, shareable detail state, or a new route/history entry;
  • reparsing Markdown in the browser, fetching another data source, lazy row loading, virtualization, or avoiding the full child payload download;
  • persistent user preference, remembering Back across visits or sessions, or making Content Detail the route-wide default;
  • a second visible or persistent hidden document reader, alternate panel, overlay, modal, or parallel view host; or
  • managed resizing/CSV behavior owned by TE-4 or diagram migration owned by TE-5.

The Table Enhancements feature owns sequencing. Content Detail View Concept And Architecture owns the shared presentation model. TE-6 begins only after TE-3 proves exact table targeting and restoration independently through explicit Open table entry.
